title: Mini dictionary query language
instructions:
Implement `parse_query(text: str) -> dict` in `query_parser.py` and
`run_query(rows: list[dict], text: str) -> list[dict]` in `query_engine.py`, using the parser.
Queries contain optional clauses in this fixed order: `where`, `select`, `order`.
Each clause can occur at most once. Empty/whitespace-only queries are valid.
Grammar (braces mean repetition, brackets mean optional):
```
[where FIELD OP VALUE {and FIELD OP VALUE}]
[select FIELD {, FIELD}]
[order FIELD asc|desc]
```
Whitespace separates words; it is optional around operators and commas. FIELD matches
`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, excluding the lowercase reserved words
`where`, `select`, `order`, `and`, `asc`, `desc`. Keywords are case-sensitive lowercase.
OP is one of `=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`. VALUE is an optionally minus-prefixed ASCII integer,
or a single/double quoted string. Strings may contain spaces, commas, operators, and the other
quote character, but not CR/LF or their own quote character. Backslashes are literal, with no
escape syntax. Integers may have leading zeros. Unquoted strings and plus signs are invalid.
A where clause requires at least one condition; select requires at least one field with no
duplicates; order requires an explicit `asc` or `desc`. Invalid syntax, unknown tokens,
unclosed strings, clause reordering, or trailing tokens raise `ValueError`.
`parse_query` returns exactly `{"where": list[tuple[str,str,int|str]], "select": list[str]|None,
"order": tuple[str,str]|None}`; absent where is `[]`, absent other clauses are None.
`run_query` filters, then sorts, then projects:
- All conditions are ANDed. A missing field or a different value type makes a condition False,
  including `!=`. Matching types use ordinary Python integer/string comparisons.
- Order is stable; missing order fields go last for both directions. Present values in an order
  field are guaranteed all integers or all strings within the input. Do not compare missing values.
- Select emits keys in the specified order; missing selected fields have value None. Without select,
  return shallow copies of complete rows. Always return a new list and new row dictionaries;
  leave the input list and dictionaries unchanged.
Input rows have string keys and only integer or string values (no booleans or None). Missing keys
are allowed. No nested values, aggregates, parentheses, OR, or expression evaluation is required.

## Files
- `query_parser.py`
- `query_engine.py`
